what: A 2px accent underline below the header menu slides to the hovered item with a 300ms swing (sine.inOut) and matches its width (item width − 25px on each side). On leaving the menu it returns to the current page item, or fades out in .3s if there is no current page. On the first hover it does not slide but appears right in place

options.ease: Curve, default sine.inOut (same as jQuery swing)
options.inset: Inset width (px) of the underline from both sides of the item, default 25
options.[data-fx-part=item]: Items the underline follows. If absent, the li children of the first list (ul) in the element
options.[data-fx-part=line]: Underline (optional) — created and attached if missing. The current page item is is-current or aria-current
options.w-dur: Duration (seconds) for the width to settle, default same as dur — brand category nav uses position .35 · width .3
options.leave: With hide, every time you leave an item (including the gap between items) it fades out instead of returning to the current page, and even while hidden it slides on to the next item — Site
options.show: Time (seconds) before the current page underline turns on at first, default 0 — brand .75
options.--fx-fade: Underline on/off duration (css variable), default .3s — brand .4s
options.--fx-fade-ease: Curve for on and off (css variable), default ease — brand ease-out

note: On devices where hover is false, like phones, only the current page underline is kept

from.where: about.html·recruit.html·page.html header line .co-gnav__line (original corporate .globalNav .line — orange 2px, jQuery animate 300ms). The site-wide set does the same job in shared.js

works.html category nav .ns-cats (ink .5px underline sitting .6em below the item — original localNavigation: transform .35s ease · inline-size .3s ease · opacity .4s ease-out, opacity 0 on item mouseleave, placed under the current item at the first 500ms · turned on at 750ms)
from.options: inset: 0; dur: .35; w-dur: .3; ease: 0.25,0.1,0.25,1; leave: hide; show: .75 · style --fx-fade: .4s; --fx-fade-ease: ease-out
